references.text: God remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, which led him to intervene to free Israel from Egypt.
The Lord promises to save Israel from slavery in Egypt with a mighty hand and great acts of judgment, fulfilling his oath to the fathers.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord brought them out of the house of bondage with a strong hand.
God identifies himself as the one who led Israel out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
God loved the fathers and chose their descendants, bringing them out of Egypt by his power.
Moses reminds that the Lord redeemed the people with his great power and brought them out with a strong hand.
The Lord took delight in the fathers and loved them, choosing their descendants.
God's oath to Abraham to bless his offspring is the foundation for the promise mentioned in Deuteronomy.
God remembered his holy word to Abraham and brought his people out with joy because he kept his covenant.
The Lord led Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm.
The Lord revealed himself to Israel with everlasting love and faithful compassion.
God's love for Israel from the time he was young, and he called his son out of Egypt.
Believers are redeemed not with silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ—an echo of the redemption from Egypt.
God's love was shown by sending his Son as an atonement for our sins—God's initiative in love.
